key_insight: Strong adverse-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers retain component-wise outer similarity when each velocity defect and Reynolds-stress component is normalized by its own value at a common outer-layer location.
engineering_relevance: The normalized profiles provide compact references for assessing APG turbulence models and reconstructing profiles when component amplitudes are known.
method: Combine direct numerical simulation of a suction–blowing-induced separation bubble with published profiles.
Normalize two mean-velocity defects and four Reynolds-stress components at a shared location, illustrated with y_s = 0.5δ.
Evaluate profile-collapse errors across reference locations and provide explicit normalized outer-profile expressions.
evidence_signal: The benchmark spans β_e = 0.04–180 and Re_θ = 530–19,000, with collapse emerging at y/δ ≳ 0.2 for velocity defects and y/δ ≳ 0.4 for Reynolds stresses.
watch_item: Component-wise collapse does not supply a universal amplitude scaling; reconstruction still requires each quantity’s value at a suitable outer-layer reference location.
paper_title: Component-wise outer similarity of turbulent boundary layers with strong adverse-pressure gradient
